History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
- 34-year-old man with new-onset breathing difficulty, lip tingling, chest tightness, and blotchy rash beginning ~15 minutes after a wasp sting; advised to initiate emergency care for possible anaphylaxis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Breathing difficulty following wasp sting.  
• Onset/duration: Sting occurred while gardening ~15 minutes prior to call; symptoms started soon afterward.  
• Course/progression: Persisting shallow breathing and chest tightness; concern for worsening.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Tingling sensation in lips (no frank swelling).  
  – No throat swelling reported.  
  – Blotchy rash present.  
  – No prior episodes of similar reactions.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None tried; has not taken medication yet.  
• Systems review: No wheeze reported; chest tightness noted. No other systems discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Eczema.  
• Allergic to penicillin (reaction details not stated).

Medications:
• Occasional antihistamine for aerosinusitis when flying (specific drug/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• No regular daily medications reported.

Social History:
• Lives with wife (present and able to assist).  
• No smoking, alcohol, or other substance details provided.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Remote consult; no vitals or physical exam performed.  
• Patient reports: lip tingling without visible swelling, blotchy skin rash, shallow breathing, chest tightness.

Investigations:
• None performed during consultation.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected allergic reaction with risk of anaphylaxis secondary to wasp sting.  
  – Advise immediate activation of emergency medical services (ambulance) rather than private transport.  
  – Instruct wife to administer available oral antihistamine while awaiting ambulance.  
  – Emphasize urgency due to potential rapid airway compromise.  
  – Recommend hospital evaluation and management, including possible epinephrine, monitoring, and further treatment.  
General plan items:  
  – Educate patient on signs of worsening (increased breathing difficulty, throat swelling, dizziness).  
  – Advise future follow-up with primary care/allergy service for insect-sting allergy evaluation after acute episode.  

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: vital signs, complete medication reconciliation, comprehensive allergy list beyond penicillin.  
• No internal conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear audio; no significant inaudible sections.
